subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: For spawned subagent runs that lose the selected Codex/OpenAI OAuth route, should OpenClaw fail closed, visibly warn and continue fallback, or keep the current logged fallback behavior after OAuth inheritance is proven?
rationale: The choice controls whether private scheduled/channel context may cross provider boundaries after auth loss, and repository policy treats auth/provider routing and fallback behavior as compatibility- and security-sensitive.

options.title: Require live proof and safer fallback policy
options.body: Keep this open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and define fail-closed or clearly visible behavior for auth-route loss.

options.title: Split visibility after proof
options.body: Close the OAuth propagation part only after live proof and track fallback warning or route-selection policy in a narrower canonical issue.

options.title: Accept logged fallback only
options.body: Maintain the existing structured-log fallback behavior after source proof, accepting the privacy and operator-surprise tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and safer fallback policy
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and define fail-closed or clearly visible behavior for auth-route loss.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent cross-surface history in auth-profile storage, OpenAI provider identity, Codex bridge context, and subagent/session routing.
